Assess the distribution for the tick 'Ixodes ricinus' in Sweden, produce a map and compare the predicted distribution for this species with the ECDC map.

**Tasks**

- Model compared to original assessment
- SDM based on another data set, with another model method and only in Sweden.
- Characterise uncertainty by model calibration where you change what data that is used (bootstrapping) and propagate to the SDM output.
- Summarise uncertainty in selected regions on the edge of the distribution
- Use your assessment to conclude if there is a concern to get bitten by a tick and become infected with tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBE). Provide your conclusion with an assessment of overall uncertainty, one per country.  

**Approach**

We use species data and habitat suitability data (climate data and land cover information) in a species distribution model(SDM).  

The modelling method is **Maxnet**, an R implementation of maximum entropy modelling. It compares the conditions at recorded locations with conditions available across the study area and it does **not** need confirmed absences.

| Choose this key | Swedish name | Scientific name | Records supplied |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"common_tick"` | Common tick | *Ixodes ricinus* | 2275 |

**Mission:**  make the maps, use the habitat suitability data and compare maps

### setting up the libraries

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", out.width = "90%")

packages <- c("SDMtune", "terra", "sf", "ggplot2", "fitdistrplus")
missing <- packages[!vapply(packages, requireNamespace, logical(1),
                            quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing)) {
  stop("Install these R packages: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}
# install.packages(c("SDMtune", "terra", "sf", "ggplot2", "fitdistrplus"))

library(SDMtune)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(fitdistrplus)
set.seed(42)  # Repeatable thinning and background sampling
```

### Add the species data 

The species data is from artportalen.se from the species Ixodes ricinus for the period 2000 - 2026, around 2275 tick observation have been recorded for Sweden.

```{r choose-species}

species_key <- "common_tick"

species <- list(
  common_tick = list(file = "Tick_data.csv",
  common = "Common tick", 
  latin = "Ixodes ricinus")
)

stopifnot(species_key %in% names(species))
tick <- species[[species_key]]
out_dir <- file.path("results", species_key)
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
tick$latin

```

## 2. Give the model a climate map and land cover map (habitat suitability data)

The habitat suitability data are two kinds of environmental maps: **climate** and **land cover**.

We use just **three** CHELSA variables so that the model and its response curves are easy to explore. They describe mean annual temperature (**BIO1**), annual precipitation (**BIO12**), and precipitation seasonality (**BIO15**). The model can learn curved relationships using linear and quadratic features.

Land cover data comes from CORINE Land Cover (CLC). Sweden is the **study area**. We crop out the neighboring countries so the background points and the final map cover the same area.

```{r NUTS-data-preparation, eval=FALSE}
nuts_all <- terra::vect("data/NUTS.gpkg") #Europe wide data 

nuts3_se <- nuts_all[nuts_all$CNTR_CODE == "SE" & nuts_all$LEVL_CODE == 3, ] #Cropping just to Sweden, Level 3 (län) region
stopifnot(nrow(nuts3_se) == 21) # sweden has 21 NUTS3 regions

terra::writeVector(nuts3_se, "data/Sweden_NUTS3.gpkg", overwrite = TRUE) #Save the cropped Sweden file as GeoPackage

terra::plot(nuts3_se, col = "#A5CCC0", border = "#294851", main = "Sweden NUTS 3 (län)")
terra::text(nuts3_se, "NUTS_ID", cex = 0.6)
```

```{r landcover-data-preparation, eval=FALSE}
landcover <- terra::rast("data/LC_Corine.tif")
nuts3_se  <- terra::vect("data/Sweden_NUTS3.gpkg")

terra::crs(landcover) <- terra::crs(nuts3_se) # lc and nuts3 data have same cordinate system

lc_sweden <- terra::mask(terra::crop(landcover, nuts3_se), nuts3_se) # cropping the lc data to sweden

terra::writeRaster(lc_sweden, "data/LC_Sweden_cropped.tif",
                   overwrite = TRUE, datatype = "INT2U") # saving the cropped raster

# Plotting the new files
terra::plot(lc_sweden, main = "Land cover, Sweden")
terra::lines(nuts3_se, col = "black")

terra::crs(lc_sweden, describe = TRUE)$name # check: should now say ETRS89-extended / LAEA Europe
```

```{r climate-data}
climate  <- terra::rast("data/climate_sweden.tif")
nuts3_se <- terra::vect("data/Sweden_NUTS3.gpkg")

stopifnot(terra::nlyr(climate) == 3)                  # the climate raster must have exactly 3 layers
names(climate) <- c("bio1", "bio12", "bio15")

nuts3_clim <- terra::vect(
  sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(nuts3_se), 4326)
) # the raster is in lon/lat and the regions in metres, so transform the regions to lon/lat (EPSG:4326)

cols <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(
  c("#143D55", "#287D91", "#A5CCC0", "#F4D392", "#D76346")
)(100)
names(climate)

terra::plot(climate[[1]], col = cols, main = "Annual mean temperature")    # map of bio1
terra::lines(nuts3_clim, col = "#294851", lwd = 0.6)

terra::plot(climate[[2]], col = cols, main = "Total annual precipitation") # map of bio12
terra::lines(nuts3_clim, col = "#294851", lwd = 0.6)

terra::plot(climate[[3]], col = cols, main = "Precipitation seasonality")  # map of bio15
terra::lines(nuts3_clim, col = "#294851", lwd = 0.6)
```

```{r landcover-data}
landcover <- terra::rast("data/LC_Sweden_cropped.tif") 
nuts3_se  <- terra::vect("data/Sweden_NUTS3.gpkg")  

names(landcover) <- "landcover"   

landcover[landcover %in% c(48, 255)] <- NA             # NODATA / unclassified codes become NA (missing)
terra::freq(landcover)                                 # values 1-44 mean GRID_CODE (the CLC legend codes)
```

```{r landcover-reclassification}
# reclassification table: from, to, becomes
rcl <- matrix(c(
   1, 11, 1,   # Artificial surfaces
  12, 22, 2,   # Agricultural areas
  23, 34, 3,   # Forest and semi natural areas
  35, 39, 4,   # Wetlands
  40, 44, 5    # Water bodies
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# right = NA makes the intervals closed on both sides, so codes 12, 23, 35 and 40 are not lost
lc_level1 <- terra::classify(landcover, rcl, include.lowest = TRUE, right = NA)
names(lc_level1) <- "lc_level1"  # new layer                   

levels(lc_level1) <- data.frame(                     
  id    = 1:5,
  class = c("Artificial surfaces", "Agricultural areas",
            "Forest and semi natural", "Wetlands", "Water bodies")
)
lc_cols <- c("red", "yellow", "forestgreen", "brown", "blue")   # one colour per class

terra::plot(lc_level1, col = lc_cols, main = "Land cover (CLC level 1)")  # map of the five classes
terra::lines(nuts3_se, col = "black", lwd = 0.6)                          # region borders on top

terra::freq(lc_level1)                                 # check: exactly 5 classes and no NA row
```
```{r forest-vegetation-layer}
# forest and vegetation = CLC GRID_CODE 23 to 29 (forests, scrub and herbaceous vegetation; CLC 311-324)
# from, to, becomes; right = NA makes the interval closed on both sides, so 23 and 29 are included
forest_sn <- terra::classify(landcover, rcl = matrix(c(23, 29, 1), ncol = 3),
                             others = 0, right = NA)   # forest and semi natural = 1, everything else = 0
names(forest_sn) <- "forest_sn"                        # name the new layer

terra::plot(forest_sn, col = c("white", "forestgreen"),
            main = "Forest and vegetation associations vs. other land")   # map of the layer (0 for non forest and 1 for forest)
terra::lines(nuts3_se, col = "black", lwd = 0.6)                      # region borders on top

terra::freq(forest_sn)                                 # number of cells in each class
```


```{r tick-observation}
records <- read.csv(file.path("data", tick$file), skip = 2, sep = ",",

stopifnot(all(c("Ost", "Nord") %in% names(records)))           # check: coordinate columns exist
records <- records[complete.cases(records[, c("Ost", "Nord")]), ]   # keep rows that have both coordinates

observations <- sf::st_as_sf(records, coords = c("Ost", "Nord"), crs = 3021)  
observations <- sf::st_transform(observations, 4326)    

regions <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_read("data/Sweden_NUTS3.gpkg", quiet = TRUE), 4326) # regional map for background

tick_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = regions, fill = "#EAF1ED",
          colour = "#91A99F", linewidth = 0.25) + # region map
  geom_sf(data = observations, colour = "#C84E3B",
          alpha = 0.45, size = 0.55) +            # observation points
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  labs(title = paste(tick$common, "|", tick$latin),

  theme_void(base_size = 12) +

```

```{r habitat-predictors}
# label the land cover and a copy of one climate layer with explicit coordinate systems
terra::crs(forest_sn) <- "+proj=laea +lat_0=52 +lon_0=10 +x_0=4321000 +y_0=3210000 +ellps=GRS80 +units=m +no_defs"
climate_grid <- climate[[1]]                              # copy of one climate layer, used only as the target grid
terra::crs(climate_grid) <- "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs"

# share of forest and semi natural land in each climate cell (0 = none, 1 = all)
forest_grid <- terra::project(forest_sn, climate_grid, method = "average")
names(forest_grid) <- "forest_grid"     # variable name 

# one stack with all predictors; NA wherever land cover is missing, so every layer covers the same cells
env <- terra::mask(c(climate, forest_grid), forest_grid)
names(env)
```



```{r fit-model}
xy <- as.data.frame(sf::st_coordinates(observations))          # tick coordinates in lon/lat
names(xy) <- c("x", "y")
presence <- as.data.frame(SDMtune::thinData(xy, env = env))    # at most one record per grid cell

background <- terra::spatSample(env[[1]], size = 2000,         # 2000 random cells across Sweden
                                method = "random", na.rm = TRUE,
                                xy = TRUE, values = FALSE)

cat("Original records:", nrow(records), "\n")
cat("Cells retained for modelling:", nrow(presence), "\n")

samples <- SDMtune::prepareSWD(species = tick$latin,           # predictor values at presence and background points
                               p = presence, a = background,
                               env = env)

# Hold back 20% of presence cells for a brief predictive check later.
parts <- SDMtune::trainValTest(samples, test = 0.2,
                               only_presence = TRUE, seed = 42)

model <- SDMtune::train(method = "Maxnet", data = parts[[1]],  # fit on the training part
                        fc = "lq", reg = 1)                    # linear + quadratic features, regularisation 1
model
```
```{r suitability-map}
suitability <- predict(model, data = env, type = "logistic")   # suitability score (0-1) for every cell, from climate + forest_grid

palette <- c("#143D55", "#287D91", "#A5CCC0", "#F4D392", "#D76346")   # blue (low) to coral (high)
map_cells <- as.data.frame(suitability, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)       # raster to a table with x, y and score
names(map_cells)[3] <- "score"                                         # name the score column

suitability_map <- ggplot(map_cells, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = score)) +
  geom_raster() +                                                       # colour each cell by its score
  geom_sf(data = sf::st_as_sf(nuts3_clim), inherit.aes = FALSE,
          fill = NA, colour = "#294851", linewidth = 0.25) +            # region borders on top
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = palette, limits = c(0, 1),
                       name = "Relative\nsuitability") +                # same colour scale for every map
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +                                # no padding, no lat/lon grid
  labs(title = "Common Tick Suitability Map for Sweden",
       subtitle = paste(tick$latin, "| Climate + forest and vegetation | Sweden"),
       caption = "Relative suitability from climate and land cover") +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, colour = "#17394A"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "#536A71"),
        plot.caption = element_text(colour = "#536A71"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.5, "cm"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))

print(suitability_map)                                                  # show the map
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "02_suitability_climate_landcover.png"),     # save it as a PNG in the results folder
       plot = suitability_map, width = 8, height = 8, dpi = 250, bg = "white")
```

```{r model-check}
test_auc  <- SDMtune::auc(model, test = parts[[2]])     # AUC on the 20% held-out presence cells
cat(sprintf("Training AUC: %.3f | Held-out AUC: %.3f\n", train_auc, test_auc))

roc_plot <- SDMtune::plotROC(model, test = parts[[2]]) +

SDMtune::plotVarImp(vi)                                 # bar chart of the importance
```

```{r orebro-suitability}
# Crop the suitability map to Orebro lan (NUTS3 code SE124): crop cuts the bounding box, mask removes cells outside the border

suitability_crop   <- terra::crop(suitability, orebro)           # cut the raster to the box around Orebro
suitability_orebro <- terra::mask(suitability_crop, orebro)      # set cells outside the real outline to NA

orebro_cells <- as.data.frame(suitability_orebro, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)   # raster to a table: x, y, suitability
```

```{r orebro-forest-cells}
# Cut the forest layer to Orebro (same grid as suitability_orebro, so cells line up)
forest_orebro <- terra::mask(terra::crop(env[["forest_grid"]], orebro), orebro)

# One row per cell with its suitability and forest share, dropping empty cells
cells <- as.data.frame(c(suitability_orebro, forest_orebro), na.rm = TRUE)   # columns: suitability, forest_grid

# Keep only forest cells: forest_threshold = minimum forest share of a cell (0.35 = at least 35 %; state this in the report)
forest_threshold <- 0.35
forest_cells <- cells[cells$forest_grid >= forest_threshold, ]
nrow(forest_cells)                                       # number of forest cells used

# Summary of the suitability values in Orebro (min, quartiles, mean, max)
summary(terra::values(suitability_orebro, na.rm = TRUE))

# Histogram of how the values are spread across the cells of Orebro
hist(terra::values(suitability_orebro, na.rm = TRUE),
     breaks = 20,                                        # number of bars
     main = "Suitability values in Orebro",              # title
     xlab = "Suitability score (0-1)")                   # x-axis label

# The inputs behind each cell's score: climate, forest share and suitability in one table
head(as.data.frame(c(suitability_orebro, env[[1:4]] |> terra::crop(orebro) |> terra::mask(orebro)),
                   xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE))             # first 6 cells; x, y are cell-centre coordinates
```


```{r fit-beta, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
# Beta needs values strictly between 0 and 1, so pull exact 0s and 1s slightly inwards
x <- pmin(pmax(forest_cells$suitability, 0.001), 0.999)

# Fit distribution to data using maximum likelihood 
fit_beta <- fitdist(x,distr= "beta", method = "mle")
# Generates plots comparing empirical cdf with fitted cdf, and histogram with fitted pdf
plot(fit_beta)
# Extract the parameters for the fitted distribution. You use these values to sample or calculate things from the distribution 
fit_beta$estimate
```

```{r fit-gamma, fig.width=8, fig.height=7 }
# Fit distribution to data using maximum likelihood 
fit_gamma <- fitdist(x,distr= "gamma", method = "mle")
plot(fit_gamma)
fit_gamma$estimate
```

```{r fit-lnorm, fig.width=8, fig.height=7 }
# Fit distribution to data using maximum likelihood 
fit_lnorm <- fitdist(x,distr= "lnorm", method = "mle")
plot(fit_lnorm)
fit_lnorm$estimate
```

```{r compare-AIC}
# Extract goodness of fit as an AIC-value and compare the three candidate models. Lower AIC is better model
AIC(fit_beta) # beta
AIC(fit_gamma) # gamma
AIC(fit_lnorm) #lnorm
```

```{r habitat-p95}
# p95 of the fitted beta distribution, Orebro forest cells 

# Read the two beta shape parameters from the fit
shape1 <- fit_beta$estimate[["shape1"]]     # first shape parameter
shape2 <- fit_beta$estimate[["shape2"]]     # second shape parameter

# 95th percentile of the fitted beta: 95% of forest cells have a suitability below this value
p95 <- qbeta(0.95, shape1 = shape1, shape2 = shape2)
p95                                          # print the value

# Check against the raw data: the empirical 95th percentile should be close to p95
quantile(x, 0.95)

# Plot the data and fitted curve, with p95 marked as a dashed line
draw_p95 <- function() {
  hist(x, breaks = 20, freq = FALSE,                       # histogram on a density scale
       main = "Suitability in forest cells, Orebro",       # title
       xlab = "Suitability score (0-1)")                   # x-axis label
  curve(dbeta(x, shape1, shape2), add = TRUE, lwd = 2)     # fitted beta curve
  abline(v = p95, lty = 2, lwd = 2)                        # dashed line at p95
}
draw_p95()                                       # show it in the report
png(file.path(out_dir, "04a_p95_Orebro.png"), width = 7, height = 5, units = "in", res = 250)
draw_p95()                                                 # draw the same plot into the file
dev.off()                                                  # close the file, which writes it to disk
```

```{r orebro-risk}
# Single risk value for Orebro: p95 suitability x prevalence

prevalence <- 0.0023                                   # prevalence of infected ticks: 0.23 % (Jaenson et al. 2014), as a proportion

# 95th percentile of the fitted beta = conservative suitability for forest cells in Orebro
HSI <- qbeta(0.95, shape1 = fit_beta$estimate[["shape1"]], shape2 = fit_beta$estimate[["shape2"]])

# Risk = P(tick | forest, region) x P(infected | tick) = P(infected | forest)
risk_orebro <- HSI * prevalence

# Print the pieces and the result
c(HSI = HSI, prevalence = prevalence, risk = risk_orebro)   # the three numbers used
round(risk_orebro * 100, 3)                           # risk as a percentage (relative indicator)
```

```{r bootstrap-risk}
# Resample the Orebro forest cells and refit the beta each time

set.seed(42)                                           # repeatable resampling
boot_beta <- fitdistrplus::bootdist(fit_beta,          # the beta fit made earlier
                                    bootmethod = "nonparam",   # resample the cells with replacement
                                    niter = 200)               # number of resamples

head(boot_beta$estim)                                  # shape1 and shape2 from each resample

# p95 of the HSI for each resample
HSI_boot <- qbeta(0.95, boot_beta$estim$shape1, boot_beta$estim$shape2)
quantile(HSI_boot, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))  # 90 % range of the p95 HSI

# --- Risk with both uncertainties: HSI bootstrap + prevalence range ---

low_prevalence  <- 0.0010           # 0.10 %, Swedish nymphs (Pettersson et al. 2014)
central_prevalence <- 0.0023        # 0.23 %, all Swedish sites (Pettersson et al. 2014)
high_prevalence <- 0.0055           # 0.55 %, Swedish adults ((Pettersson et al. 2014)

set.seed(42)                                            # repeatable prevalence draws
prevalence_draw <- runif(length(HSI_boot),              # one prevalence value for each bootstrap round
                         low_prevalence, high_prevalence)

risk_all <- HSI_boot * prevalence_draw                  # risk for each round: its HSI x its prevalence

quantile(risk_all, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))                  # 90 % range of the risk, both uncertainties

# Which uncertainty matters more? Compare the three ranges
risk_table <- rbind(
  HSI_only      = quantile(HSI_boot * central_prevalence,      c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95)),   # HSI varies, prevalence fixed
  prevalence_only = quantile(median(HSI_boot) * prevalence_draw, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95)),   # prevalence varies, HSI fixed
  both            = quantile(risk_all,                           c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))    # both vary
)
risk_table                                             # print the table

# --- Histogram: show it and save it ---

risk_percent <- risk_all * 100                             # risk as a percentage
q <- quantile(risk_percent, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))            # 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles

draw_hist <- function() {                              # one function so the same plot is shown and saved
  hist(risk_percent, breaks = 30,
       main = "Risk in Orebro (HSI bootstrap + prevalence range)", xlab = "Risk (%)")
  abline(v = q[c(1, 3)], col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)   # red dashed lines: 5th and 95th percentile
  abline(v = q[2], col = "red", lty = 1, lwd = 2)         # solid red line: median
  legend("topright", legend = c("Median", "5th and 95th percentile"),
         col = "red", lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
}

draw_hist()                                            # show it in the report

png(file.path(out_dir, "04_risk_histogram_Orebro.png"), width = 7, height = 5, units = "in", res = 250)
draw_hist()                                            # draw the same plot into the file
dev.off()                                              # close the file, which writes it to disk

# Save the numbers too
write.csv(round(risk_table, 6), file.path(out_dir, "risk_table_Orebro.csv"))   # the three ranges
```

```{r maxnet-bootstrapping, cache=TRUE}
# --- Model Bootstrapping & Propagation to SDM Output ---

n_boots <- 200        # Number of bootstrap iterations 
boot_list <- vector("list", n_boots)

set.seed(42)
for (i in seq_len(n_boots)) {
  # 1. Resample presence points with replacement
  boot_presence <- presence[sample(nrow(presence), replace = TRUE), ]
  
  # 2. Resample background points with replacement (or sample fresh background points)
  boot_background <- terra::spatSample(env[[1]], size = 2000, 
                                       method = "random", na.rm = TRUE,
                                       xy = TRUE, values = FALSE)
  
  # 3. Prepare SWD object for the bootstrap sample
  boot_samples <- SDMtune::prepareSWD(species = tick$latin,
                                     p = boot_presence, 
                                     a = boot_background,
                                     env = env)
  
  # 4. Train Maxnet model on bootstrapped data
  boot_model <- SDMtune::train(method = "Maxnet", data = boot_samples,
                               fc = "lq", reg = 1)
  
  # 5. Predict spatial suitability map for this iteration
  boot_list[[i]] <- predict(boot_model, data = env, type = "logistic")
  
  if (i %% 50 == 0) cat(sprintf("Completed bootstrap iteration %d of %d\n", i, n_boots))   # progress every 50 rounds
}

# Combine all individual prediction rasters into a single SpatRaster stack
boot_stack <- terra::rast(boot_list)
names(boot_stack) <- paste0("boot_", seq_len(n_boots))
```

```{r risk-maps}
# --- Risk maps for Orebro: Maxnet bootstrap maps x prevalence draws ---

cols_risk <- colorRampPalette(c("#143D55", "#287D91", "#A5CCC0", "#F4D392", "#D76346"))(100)   # low to high risk
cols_unc  <- colorRampPalette(c("white", "#F4D392", "#D76346", "#7A1F13"))(100)                 # low to high uncertainty

boot_stack_orebro <- terra::mask(terra::crop(boot_stack, orebro), orebro)   # cut the bootstrap maps to Orebro

stopifnot(length(prevalence_draw) == terra::nlyr(boot_stack_orebro))        # one prevalence value per bootstrap map

risk_stack <- terra::rast(lapply(seq_len(terra::nlyr(boot_stack_orebro)), function(i) {
  boot_stack_orebro[[i]] * prevalence_draw[i]                               # suitability map x its prevalence draw
}))

risk_mean <- terra::mean(risk_stack)                                        # best-estimate risk per cell
risk_sd   <- terra::stdev(risk_stack)                                       # uncertainty of the risk per cell

# Save the plot
png(file.path(out_dir, "05_risk_maps_Orebro.png"), width = 10, height = 5, units = "in", res = 250)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
terra::plot(risk_mean, col = cols_risk, main = "Mean risk (Orebro)")
terra::lines(orebro, col = "#294851", lwd = 1)
terra::plot(risk_sd, col = cols_unc, main = "Uncertainty of risk (SD)")
terra::lines(orebro, col = "#294851", lwd = 1)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
dev.off()

# Display the plot in the knitted report
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
terra::plot(risk_mean, col = cols_risk, main = "Mean risk (Orebro)")
terra::lines(orebro, col = "#294851", lwd = 1)
terra::plot(risk_sd, col = cols_unc, main = "Uncertainty of risk (SD)")
terra::lines(orebro, col = "#294851", lwd = 1)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

terra::writeRaster(risk_mean, file.path(out_dir, "risk_mean_Orebro.tif"), overwrite = TRUE)   # mean risk raster
terra::writeRaster(risk_sd,   file.path(out_dir, "risk_sd_Orebro.tif"),   overwrite = TRUE)   # uncertainty raster
```
